topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and frames the importance and complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations and core principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide the essential background, nomenclature rules, and central C3 activation concept required to understand the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the alternative, lectin, and classical recognition pathways initiate complement activation to reach a shared convertase threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the functional mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates pathogens via opsonization, inflammatory signaling, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host tissues from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the distinct disease presentations and clinical vulnerabilities resulting from deficiencies in various complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens to subvert complement defenses, focusing on the mechanisms of Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session on complement and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
